The leak path is upstream and real: wgcna_dirs/wgcna_find take scope as an unvalidated free string (wgcna_paths.R:71-76, 110), so scope = "microglia_failed_20260720_133211" builds a perfectly legal normalized module_score path; and score_module_activity.R:180 already resolves its overlap definitions with resolve_input_path(latest_roots = path_results("tables","06_modules_WGCNA"), latest_pattern = ...), which is an mtime-ranked list.files(recursive = TRUE) over the whole stage root (R/paths.R:382-393, 471) and therefore does traverse the failed-run directory. Separately, raw-vs-adjudicated labels are NOT a risk inside this family: module_score tables carry raw Module/ModuleID and the adjudicated label is joined in by the readers from WGCNA_final_label_lookup.csv (summarize_module_scores.R:449 via canonical_final_label_lookup; render_module_circular_atlas.R:295, :2929), which is the separate interpretable_summary family served by wgcna_final_label_lookup(). Bilateral-vs-hemisphere is also not native here: module_score headers carry Region/Layer/RegionLayer/SpatialUnit and no Hemisphere column; the hemisphere-resolved values are the group_effects family (WGCNA_group_effect_hemisphere_values.csv, pipeline.yml:437). The aggregation axis that IS confusable here is Sample vs AnimalID x RegionLayer, and primary_all_replicates vs sensitivity_flagged_replicates_removed, which sit side by side in the same directory as module_scores_per_sample.csv vs module_scores_per_sample_sensitivity_flagged_replicates_removed.csv - one more reason to name files explicitly and never resolve this family at directory granularity.

object_identity_risk: Five concrete ways a careless resolver returns the wrong object. (1) Corrected-vs-uncorrected prefix collision: results/figures/06_modules_WGCNA/wgcna_publication_figures_corrected/microglia is a DIFFERENT scientific object owned by a DIFFERENT analysis_id (render_microglia_module_figures, pipeline.yml:534+; config/results_ownership.csv:19,140). Any startsWith/glob on "wgcna_publication_figures" matches the corrected tree; its labels are the post-correction unsuffixed adjudicated labels (asserted at tests/testthat/test-wgcna-reviewed-label-registry.R:138-155: canonical_short_label and roi_context present) while the uncorrected forest/spatial sources are asserted NOT to carry them - so a prefix match silently substitutes corrected labels into an uncorrected panel or vice versa. wgcna_paths.R itself is safe here (wg_legacy_root does exact file.path joins, no prefix match), but any hand-rolled grepl/startsWith reader is not. (2) Same basename in two historical namespaces: <stem>_source.csv exists BOTH at results/tables/06_modules_WGCNA/wgcna_publication_figures/microglia/ and results/source_data/06_modules_WGCNA/wgcna_publication_figures/microglia/ (write_figure_source, render_module_figures.R:70-73, writes both). legacy_family = "tables" vs "source_data" returns different files with identical names. Worse, the natural-looking call wgcna_find(..., child = "tables", "source_data") is wrong: wgcna_artifact_candidates appends the trailing ... to BOTH candidates (wgcna_paths.R:118-128), so the legacy candidate becomes .../wgcna_publication_figures/microglia/source_data/<file>, a directory that has never existed; nothing matches and wgcna_find silently returns the not-yet-written normalized path, making the caller report a missing input for a file that is on disk. (3) Immutability erasure at audit_microglia_module_claims.R:122: results/wgcna/render_module_figures/ does not exist yet (verified: absent on disk). If line 122 is repointed with a bare canonical_result_path() instead of wgcna_dir_any, dir.exists() is FALSE (or the dir is an empty create=TRUE skeleton), list.files returns character(0), the figure rows drop out of protected_files, and all(protected_after$unchanged) over zero figure rows is TRUE (line 1639) - the protected_outputs_unchanged gate passes while protecting nothing. wgcna_dir_any is the safe form precisely because wg_has_files() (wgcna_paths.R:58-63) refuses an empty normalized skeleton. (4) Failed-run scope leakage: microglia_failed_20260720_133211 exists as a sibling scope under results/tables/06_modules_WGCNA/01_WGCNA/ and data/processed/06_modules_WGCNA/01_WGCNA/ but NOT under wgcna_publication_figures (only "microglia"). A resolver that scope-globs microglia* , or that forwards an unvalidated scope taken from an upstream state path, finds no historical candidate and falls back to results/wgcna/render_module_figures/microglia_failed_20260720_133211/plots - a path no producer will ever write, so the export/oracle sees an empty family instead of erroring. (5) Bilateral vs hemisphere vs spatial substitution: these figures are built from all_supermodule_eigengene_group_values.csv and supermodule_pca_member_loadings.csv (bilateral, equal hemisphere weighting after within-hemisphere technical-row means - pipeline.yml:466 notes), while the same group_effects directory also holds WGCNA_group_effect_hemisphere_values.csv and all_supermodule_eigengene_spatial_group_values.csv. Serving this family through wgcna_group_effects_dir() rather than the render_module_figures family returns hemisphere-resolved or spatial-unit values in place of the bilateral figure source.
